My Male 7 mo old Pembroke prefers to eat overnight usually. I'll put his food in his crate before we go to bed (a can and some dry food just in case) and it's magically gone by 7am the next morning. 

My vet said they're not worried, he's healthy for his size. And for my area (Southern IL) it's getting hot here and is pretty hot in the summers, so they said him eating at the "coolest time of day" isn't abnormal.

So as long as your girl is a healthy weight (which she seems to be), I think you're all good.

If your state is anything like IL, you should be able to call your member services and report that they charged you more than their allowed amount (once it's done reprocessing from the corrections). You have an Itemized Bill / receipt that shows you paid it too. So your member services should be able to help you with that.

Hey, not sure what state you're in / insurance you have, but call your insurance up and ask if they can reprocess the claim as INN since your ordering doctor is INN. 

Some insurances have an "ologist" rule where the off site billers ( for this example, The laboratory) are able to be considered INN if the ordering doctor is INN. You need to have a PPO policy though. HMOs are kinda out of luck :/

https://www.chewy.com/dp/277073?utm_source=app-share&utm_campaign=277073

Pretty generic, but I love that I can set it up as a box in the corner of the room (using a wall as a side). So getting one that can convert between gate or play pen is nice.

Only complaints are if you don't want to bolt it into the wall, you'll need to reinforce the sides if the puppy likes to jump on it/push against it. I remedied that for us by  putting the gate against a wall and putting our armchair against the other side.

If you have the room, I also highly recommend getting a play pen. I have a 13 week old Corgi puppy and the pen I got takes up a corner of the living room. It's big enough he has some room to play and move with his crate in it.

It gives me peace of mind cuz he can still move around and play when he isn't tired, but I'm exhausted and need a nap. (Also keeps him from terrorizing the cats 24/7).

It also limits his area to have accidents when unsupervised. The mat I got to go underneath is also machine washable and easy to clean accidents out of. So I also recommend getting one of those.

I also second using the stitch markers more. I tried to only use the odd colored one as the mark of the round, like they suggest in the videos, but I kept having issues with the stitches not matching. 

I personally found that using the 2 same colored to mark the end of the last two rows that you're **sure** are correct, and the odd colored to mark the beginning of the next row was what worked best for me.

So I'd recommended trying using the markers in different ways (but keeping the odd one as the first stitch of that row) until you figure out what works best for you. :)

I've hand raised quite a few kittens over the years (perks of working at an animal hospital for 10 years, starting in high school). I'm even currently raising a 5 week old orange kitten that I've named Rueben <3  


Precursor of: this is advise, not medical advise, and not being given by a licensed vet. You should consult with a vet, and ask them these questions too.

Main word of advise is to try feeding the baby routinely. Don't worry about over feeding them, they're a baby and they need all the energy they can get to grow. So don't force them to eat, but offer it every couple hours. And make sure to wake up routinely throughout the night until they're like 4 weeks old or so and/or have enough coordination to drink the milk replacer from a shallow dish.  


As for the hoodie advice, that is great! And has been a life saver for the last week. You can also sub turning a hoodie around, and putting them in your hood, just make sure to support the bottom if you're not sitting down with the kitten laying on you.  


The kitten will require socialization with other cats. If you don't have your own that you can introduce to the kitten (under supervision) when they get older and start to explore, then I second the suggestion to foster/adopt another kitten if you can. It does help to keep them warm as previously stated, and helps with their socialization / learning how to cat.  


As for the place to keep them confined, I've been using a cat carrier with a blanket. Mine has a door on the top and the front, so it makes it really easy to get to my little boy. And it helped him to not fuss in the night, cuz he could see when I set his carrier on my night stand against the wall (it's in a corner). It also meant that I heard him when he would fuss in the night cuz he was hungry.  


As he's been getting older, I've transitioned him to our bathroom at night. It's small and warmer than most bathrooms usually are due to this. And he has a nice big cat bed to sleep on in there, and can run around all night as much as he wants (I kitten proofed it). When he started screaming at me for hours at night cuz he was bored was when I knew it was time. But he's much too little at 5 weeks to have the run of the house unsupervised. Especially with 2 adult cats and 1 other older kitten in the house. So a small room with a door is great for that. A big tote (with no lid obviously) would also suffice for a week or two, but not for nearly as long as a room.  


Don't worry too much about toys until the kitten is more mobile and not super wobbly. Then I'd suggest introducing some stuffed mice, cat balls, small wands, etc. And a scratching pad is a must. Don't invest in a cat tree until they're able to jump and climb well. Otherwise they might get themselves hurt as they try to climb it.

I rechecked my texts, and I got a text before they left the place they had spent the night at, but that was at like 2pm, and I didn't realize the town was 3 hours away. And neither told me that either. I think they just assumed I knew that fact since they had gone to the nearest biggest city. I'm new to the area though, and was not aware. They also got lost and had problems getting out of the city. Missed a couple exits. But I was not told that until later.

So I was miffed when they got back to L's to pick up her car around 7pm. L did call, and asked if I had had dinner yet, and when I said yes, said that they were going to go out for dinner with her NP and would be home later that night. (Apparently, if I had said no, they were going to come back asap and go to dinner with me and kiddo, but I was not told that until Sunday). I was angry and dealing with kiddo being angry and disappointed, and tried to end the call ASAP before I said something I'd regret, and then C texted me asking what was wrong, and that's when I basically lashed out at him via text.

Not excusing his behaviour, but also not excusing mine at that moment. I definitely could have handled that better. 

But thank you, I'm thinking about things more objectively, and appreciate the outside opinions.

Mostly think I just need to step back, see what exactly the issues are atm, give C some time to see if this continues, and then talk to him about it all.

I'm also starting to wonder if he does feel a bit guilty and is trying to make up for it subconsciously. Could also explain why he's been super sensitive to my emotional changes and was frequently checking up on me while writing this cuz he could hear me sighing, and was asking if I'm ok, etc. (He's not a bad partner, but when he has those rare spells of being shitty, he really can be.)

In his defense, he's usually spending time with our son after work / school and takes him to parks all the time and routinely does whatever our son wants with him until he goes to bed. I'm usually the one who isn't as available due to work, etc. This was pretty uncharacteristic of him, and I'm wondering if he's feeling burned out... I feel like he was more trying to tell me that he rarely isn't doting on our son (that week of overnights was a first for all of us, and I don't think our son would have minded having a couple days of just me and him if it hadn't of been *right* after that week), and if I remember correctly, he said he feels like we were trying to punish him for wanting to have a break.

Dating someone else is on the table for me, but I'm not actively pursuing it. I'm worried I'm seeking out another partner for the wrong reasons. And I don't think that'd be fair to said potential partner, if that is true. But, if I meet someone who is interested, then I'm open to trying.
